items.stem: Test H₀:X~Uniform(0,1) against H₁:X~N(0,1), at level α with 0<α<1. Which statements are correct?
statements: A most powerful test exists for every α in (0,1).
A most powerful test fails to exist for some α in (0,1).
items.explanation: The Neyman–Pearson lemma gives a most powerful test. Under H₀ the support is (0,1), but under H₁ the normal density is positive on the whole real line. Thus the test must reject outside (0,1), where rejection costs no size. Within (0,1), the likelihood ratio φ(x) decreases for x>0, so the remaining size α is assigned to 0<x≤α. The full region is (−∞,0]∪(0,α]∪[1,∞), up to boundary conventions. The two regions printed in C and D omit the alternative-only support, so only A is true as written.

A.why: The Neyman–Pearson likelihood-ratio ordering supplies an MP test for every prescribed size.

B.why: A most powerful test exists for each 0<α<1.

C.why: The displayed set omits x≤0 and x≥1, where H₀ has zero density and H₁ has positive density.

D.why: This is also incomplete and uses the wrong cutoff within the null support.

items.repaired: The scan marks A and C. Statement C is incomplete as a full rejection region; the correct region also rejects outside the null support.
